selected_leaf.tested_scope: Self-local deterministic three-event replay for repository-id-bound create-once claims with old claimant A at generation 7, takeover claimant B at generation 8, a client-side exact fence read by A, and no atomic commit-time expected branch-head/fence precondition. No O/downstream/other-worker semantic input, public web, live claim mutation, issue/PR/review mutation, scheduler mutation, wait, polling, retry, or optional second leaf was used.
selected_leaf.observation: The interleaving A_read(fence=7) -> B_takeover(write fence=8) -> A_commit contains a stale post-takeover commit: A's last exact read still authorizes its client logic, and without a server-enforced precondition coupled to the effect commit, B's intervening takeover is not atomically checked at A_commit.
selected_leaf.falsification: A monotonically increasing role-local generation/fence plus pre-commit exact readback alone does not prevent a stale claimant from committing after takeover when the effect mutation is not atomically conditioned on that fence or on the branch head.
selected_leaf.inference: Strict stale-commit prevention requires a commit-time atomic precondition tied to the active fence/lease or branch head. A generation-scoped append-only output plus active-generation pointer can instead make stale commits non-authoritative if every consumer rejects generations other than the current pointer, but that weakens the property from 'prevent stale commit' to 'prevent stale effect acceptance' and therefore does not close the strict fencing child.
